key_insight: Re-TRAC compresses each agent trajectory into a structured, recursive state summary so LLM-based agents can revisit, branch, and reason across trajectories—breaking the linear ReAct chain to avoid local optima and redundant exploration.
problem_solved: Linear ReAct-style traces make it hard for agents to maintain global awareness, revisit earlier states, or branch into alternative search directions, which causes inefficient search, redundant work, and stagnation in local optima.
method: After each trajectory, generate a structured state representation that captures evidence, actions, outcomes, and uncertainty.
Recursively compress and index these state summaries to enable cross-trajectory retrieval, branching, and re-entry into prior search points.
Use the compressed summaries to guide planning and prioritization (uncertainty-guided exploration and targeted re-examination), reducing context burden and redundant exploration.
impact: Re-TRAC makes deep search agents more efficient, scalable, and interpretable by enabling non-linear exploration and global state awareness—leading to faster convergence, less wasted computation, and better handling of long-context tasks.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: linear ReAct timeline vs. Re-TRAC recursive trajectory tree to show branching and revisitation
Flowchart showing: trajectory -> structured state summary -> compression/indexing -> cross-trajectory retrieval -> guided next-step planning
Heatmap or bar chart comparing search efficiency metrics (time-to-solution, redundant steps, success rate) between ReAct and Re-TRAC
Annotated example trace: a compressed state card showing evidence, uncertainty, and suggested branches
paper_title: RE-TRAC: REcursive TRAjectory Compression for Deep Search Agents
paper_authors: Jialiang Zhu, Gongrui Zhang, Xiaolong Ma, Lin Xu, Miaosen Zhang
